ResearchProjectDef.label: demonic archaeology
ResearchProjectDef.description: Fragments of a devil arm turn up in a ruin, and the metallurgy makes no sense: an alloy that was never smelted, holding an edge it was never given. Working out how the thing is put together is the first step. It will not tell you how to wake one up - that comes later - but it is enough to build a competent copy of the simpler ones.\n\nUnlocks Rebellion and the Coyote-A.

ResearchProjectDef.label: legendary weapon forging
ResearchProjectDef.description: The alloy is not the interesting part. What matters is that a devil arm is a demon that lost an argument and was folded into a shape - which means the forging process is less metallurgy than it is negotiation. Once you can hold something down long enough to hammer it flat, most of the named arms become reproducible.\n\nUnlocks the bulk of the arsenal, elemental arms included.

ResearchProjectDef.label: ultimate demon armaments
ResearchProjectDef.description: The arms at the top of the list were not forged so much as agreed to. Sparda's own blade, the two devil swords, the king of Fire Hell - each of these was a being of some standing before it was equipment, and building a working copy means reproducing not just the shape but whatever it was that convinced the original to hold still.\n\nUnlocks the devil swords, Sparda, Balrog, Gilgamesh and the Cavaliere.
